bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change and extreme-weather damage to telecom infrastructure (rated 'Strategic', outlook from last year: Emerging) — Natural disasters have severely impacted livelihoods and infrastructure including telecommunication infrastructure. Climate-related risks may degrade telecom infrastructure, adversely affect service availability and quality, increase business costs, impact maintenance and repair operations and pose health and safety risks to personnel. The Company has responded with a climate-resilience plan setting design criteria for flood-prone, water-scarce, cyclone/wind-prone and high-temperature areas.
- Geographic concentration in two circles with no international operations — The Company serves only the Rajasthan and North-East telecommunication circles - the North-East comprising Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura - and Bharti Hexacom has no international operations, with exports contributing 0.14% of turnover. Regional economic, weather or competitive shocks cannot be diversified away.
- Revenue concentration in wireless telecommunication activity — Wireless telecommunication activities contribute 95.93% of total turnover against 4.07% from wired telecommunication activities, so the earnings base is exposed to a single technology and regulatory regime; the customer base is end consumers (B2C).
- Structural dependence on the holding company, Bharti Airtel Limited — Bharti Airtel Limited is the holding company; the ESG regime of Bharti Hexacom operates under the group-wide regime of Bharti Airtel, and BHL adheres to the SOPs and methodologies for core KPIs, metrics and Scope 3 accounting developed and maintained by Bharti Airtel. Governance, methodology and disclosure quality are therefore inherited rather than independently controlled.
- Information security, data privacy and cyber risk amid a shifting regulatory landscape — The Internal Auditor and Internal Assurance Partners report information security risk to the Audit Committee on a quarterly basis. The Company's privacy framework is being revised in response to recent updates under the DPDPA, including anticipated guidance on the classification of Significant Data Fiduciaries and associated obligations.
- Employee attrition — Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 25.2% in FY 2025-26 (26.1% male, 19.1% female) from 19.9% in FY 2024-25 and 19.3% in FY 2023-24, a material step-up in churn for a business dependent on network and commercial execution.
- Limits on physical verification of a distributed asset base — The statutory auditors commented on updation of quantitative and situation details for certain fixed assets, and on the absence of physical verification of customer premises equipment, bandwidth and optic fibre cable. Network equipment is moved between site locations on an urgent basis to keep the network running, with the situation updated in the Fixed Assets Register only afterwards - an inherent control weakness in asset tracking.
- Regulatory and compliance exposure across telecom, listing and cost-audit regimes — The Company is subject to SEBI Listing Regulations, the Companies Act 2013 (including CSR under Section 135 and cost records under Section 148(1)), TRAI's Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal Regulation 2012, and SEBI's BRSR/BRSR Core disclosure regime with third-party assurance. Compliance, statutory and reporting risks are reported quarterly to the Audit Committee, and a statutory auditor transition is due on conclusion of the 32nd AGM in calendar 2027.

outlook.body:
- Convergence: bring mobility, broadband, Digital TV and digital services together within a unified ecosystem to deepen customer relationships, raise share among high-value homes and lift customer lifetime value
- Expand the 5G footprint, deepen rural connectivity and modernise network capabilities, supported by a robust spectrum portfolio
- Scale Home Broadband through continued expansion of Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) and Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), with FWA used to accelerate broadband penetration in markets with relatively weaker fibre presence
- Rural Acceleration Programme: continue rolling out sites in underserved rural areas to unlock access to digital commerce and payments
- Maintain a dual-mode 5G network supporting both Standalone (SA) and Non-Standalone (NSA) configurations as a future-ready foundation for network slicing and low-latency applications
- Embed Artificial Intelligence across operations - network operations simplification, intelligent capacity planning, smart site deployment, energy optimisation and predictive field engineering support - and deploy AI-powered anti-spam solutions
- Portfolio premiumisation and a disciplined focus on customer quality, improving the mix of acquisitions to drive ARPU growth
- Strengthen the content proposition for the home through regional and global partnerships and the launch of IPTV
- Pursue the stated corporate objectives of growing market share, growing revenue and driving down cost, with the vision of enriching customers' lives and winning customers for life through an exceptional experience
- Leverage digital capabilities of the parent, Bharti Airtel, rather than building them standalone
- Capital allocation is governed by a formal policy architecture rather than a stated numeric payout. The Dividend Distribution Policy 'provides guidance on the factors considered while declaring payment of dividend, scenarios where dividend will not be paid, etc.', and sits alongside the Policy on Materiality and Dealing in Related Party Transactions, which governs identification and approval of transactions with related parties - material given the Company's dependence on the holding company for purchases. The RPT Policy requires prior Audit Committee approval for all related party transactions, with additional prior Board approval where a Director or KMP is interested, and the interested Director recuses himself/herself from discussion and voting. Investment decisions carry an explicit sustainability tilt: a small but disclosed share of total capex is directed to technologies that improve environmental and social impact (replacing old servers with energy-efficient models, deploying battery banks and solar panels to lower diesel dependency, and implementing SPAM 2.0 with GTI Advanced for real-time fraud and spam protection), and sustainable sourcing procedures cover the large majority of inputs. An Enterprise Risk Management Framework defines identification, prioritisation, mitigation and reporting of key risks along with the roles of the Board and its Committees.
- BRSR Core KPIs across nine ESG attributes - GHG footprint, water footprint, energy footprint, circularity/waste management, employee wellbeing and safety, gender diversity, inclusive development, fairness in engaging with customers and suppliers, and openness of business - are reported under reasonable assurance from DNV Business Assurance India Private Limited, with limited assurance over the remaining BRSR disclosures
- A documented climate-resilience plan to build and re-engineer telecom infrastructure, with specific design criteria for flood-prone areas (lean tower designs with elevated platform foundations, raised plinths, siting built on Central Water Commission historical flood data, elevated access pathways, flood-resistant materials, swales and drainage, early flood warning systems, retrofit of vulnerable electrical assets)
- Cyclone- and wind-prone design criteria: removal of Cells on Wheels, microwave and unsafe towers in favour of permanent structures, RRUs mounted behind base station antennas to cut wind exposure, avoidance of microwave dishes over 1.2m diameter, V clamps in place of U clamps, tower loading per design document, structural safety certification for rooftop towers and regular structural health assessments
- Water-scarce area design criteria including blue roofs, rainwater harvesting and reuse, greywater recycling, wastewater heat recovery, water-efficient fixtures and leak detection systems
- Temperature-related design criteria including white/reflective roofs, green roofs and vegetation, improved glazing and external shading, and heat-resistant materials
- Scope 1 GHG emissions calculated using 2006 IPCC Guidelines, IPCC sixth assessment report, TRAI's Approach towards Sustainable Telecommunications, UK Defra 2025 factors and GHG Protocol cross-sector factors; Scope 2 for Indian operations calculated on the CEA grid emission factor (Version 21.0) of 0.710 kg CO2/kWh, quantified on a market-based approach in line with the GHG Protocol
- As a group company, BHL adheres to Bharti Airtel Limited's documented SOPs, calculation approaches, assumptions, exclusions, materiality assessment criteria and Scope 3 accounting procedures
- Policies cover all nine NGRBC principles, are Board-approved, translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners, with performance against policies reviewed annually and statutory compliance reviewed quarterly; the Board holds ultimate oversight of all ESG matters and the ESG regime operates under the group-wide regime of Bharti Airtel Limited
- Independent external assessment of the working of the Company's policies has been carried out across all nine principles
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for every stakeholder group - Communities and NGOs (Communities & NGOs Grievance Redressal Policy), shareholders/investors, employees and workers, customers (Telecom Customer Charter, with resolution and reporting under TRAI's Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal Regulation, 2012), suppliers (Airtel Partner World) and channel partners (Anmol Ratna Portal)
- CSR policy focused on education for underprivileged children in rural areas, health and sanitation programmes and rural development projects, overseen by a CSR Committee constituted under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Annual Report sections routed here do not disclose a discrete plant or project pipeline - Bharti Hexacom is a licensed telecom services operator offering mobile, fixed-line telephone, Wi-Fi and IPTV across the Rajasthan and North-East circles, and the expansion agenda is expressed as a widening of the permitted business scope rather than as a physical capacity build. The principal forward step is a Special Resolution placed before the 31st AGM (Tuesday, August 11, 2026) to amend the main object clause of the Memorandum of Association, substituting sub-clause 1 of Clause III(A) so that the Company may establish, operate, maintain or expand telecommunication networks under the Telecommunication Act, 2023 across a materially broader set of services. The proposed clause explicitly covers unified and access services (mobile and fixed line/wireline), satellite-based telecommunication services, wireless and wireline access networks, internet services, national and international long-distance and international SIM services, internet telephony, enterprise communication, leased circuits and Internet Lease Lines, Machine-to-Machine (M2M), DTH and IPTV, Aeronautical Data Communication, In-Flight and Maritime Connectivity (IFMC), Captive Non-Public Networks (CNPN), PMRTS, cloud-based EPABX and Wi-Fi services, and captive telecom services. It also extends to telecommunication infrastructure activity as an Infrastructure Provider (IP) and Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Provider (DCIP) - dark fibre, rights-of-way, duct space, towers, poles, IBS infrastructure and associated equipment for wireline access networks, Radio Access Network (RAN), WLAN and transmission links - plus establishing and operating Internet Exchange Points (IXPs), Satellite Earth Station Gateways (SESGs) and related baseband systems, Network-as-a-Service (NaaS), Cloud-hosted Telecommunication Networks (CTNs) and CTN-as-a-Service, mobile number portability, and future-generation services such as 5G and 6G including OTT/multimedia delivery, satellite-based, cloud-native, virtualised, software-defined, non-terrestrial, AI-enabled and quantum-safe offerings. On the asset side, the Company operates a rolling programme of physical verification of fixed assets structured to cover all items over a period of three years, with network equipment moved between site locations on an urgent basis to keep the network running and each movement's situation subsequently updated in the Fixed Assets Register; customer premises equipment, bandwidth and optic fibre cable are not physically verified given their nature and location. Funding-side flexibility is being preserved through a Material Related Party Transactions approval with holding company Bharti Airtel Limited under Regulation 23(4) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, also tabled at the 31st AGM.

outlook.body:
- Wireless penetration in Rajasthan and the North-East still lags the national average, leaving significant headroom for long-term growth
- Domestic broadband penetration is still at a nascent stage across the circles served, which FWA is being used to address as a significant untapped opportunity
- Rising smartphone penetration and an improving customer mix support mobility momentum; smartphone data customers now account for 79% of the mobile base
- Data consumption grew 28% during the year, supporting continued network monetisation
- Government investment in digital infrastructure in both circles, Rajasthan's Vision 2047 development ambitions and the North-East's role as India's gateway to ASEAN under the Act East Policy are accelerating digital adoption
- A growing tourism industry in the regions adds to demand for connectivity
- The regulatory environment remains constructive - TRAI has provided a stable and enabling policy framework while remaining responsive to industry concerns
- India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, anchored in robust domestic consumption despite tariff-related disruption, trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical tension in West Asia
- Continued 5G adoption plus sustained rural expansion is strengthening the Company's market position
- Life-time high revenue market share across the two circles, up 925 basis points over five years to 46%, reflecting sustained investment and execution

one-line thesis: Bharti Hexacom, as the digital infrastructure arm of Bharti Airtel, is strategically scaling high-margin adjacencies—data centers, sovereign cloud, and financial services—while optimizing core telecom capex and leveraging AI to drive operational efficiency and customer retention, positioning it for sustained EBITDA margin expansion and free cash flow growth.
financial scorecard: rev: +2.6% QoQ; EBITDA: 52% margin; PAT: Not disclosed; orderbook: +17% YoY; netdebt: 1.1x EBITDAaL
guidance: No explicit guidance provided; management indicates capex will remain in 'ballpark' of FY26 levels, with disciplined allocation prioritizing core network, fiber, data centers, and adjacencies.
order book & pipeline: B2B order book grew 17% YoY in FY26; strong funnel in IoT, security, cloud, and Nxtra; multiple enterprise wins secured in Q4.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mobile: ARPU Rs.257 (+Rs.3 QoQ), 4.7M net adds (5.8M smartphones); Homes: 1.1M net adds, 45M home passes, IPTV adoption driving turnaround; B2B: Rs.5,500Cr revenue (+2.6% QoQ); Data Centers: Nxtra raising $1B, 1GW ambition; Financial Services: Airtel Money NBFC approved, Rs.550Cr/month loan disbursement; Airtel Cloud: 24 deals secured, sovereign positioning; Payments Bank: 120M monthly transacting users, Rs.3,400Cr annualized revenue.
growth verticals / optionality: Data centers (1GW ambition), sovereign cloud (India-first compliance), Airtel Money NBFC commercial launch, fiber-to-home expansion (45M+ passes), AI monetization via digital services, and potential listing of Airtel Money or Nxtra.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDAaL margin improved to 52% in Q4; cost pressures from memory/servers mitigated via 'War on Waste'; diesel reduction and renewable energy (42,000 solarized sites) improving opex efficiency.
capex / expansion: India capex (ex-passive): Rs.31,000Cr in FY26; wireless capex at 16% of sales (decade low); focus shifting to transport (fiber), edge data centers (56 planned), and data center expansion; no material increase expected unless 5G densification demands arise.
capital allocation: Prioritized: 1) Core network (fiber, 5G), 2) Adjacencies (data centers, cloud, fintech), 3) Deleveraging (net debt/EBITDA 1.1x), 4) Progressive dividends (Rs.24/share, +50% YoY); no cash outflows for Africa (share swap), no non-India acquisitions planned.
risks & watch-items: Global supply chain (memory/chip shortages), energy price inflation, geopolitical impact on international roaming, regulatory delays in fintech, competition in cloud/data centers, and slow ARPU recovery without tariff reform.
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined; strong emphasis on operational excellence, AI integration, and long-term adjacencies; tone on ARPU is urgent but pragmatic, acknowledging pricing architecture is 'broken' but not imminent to fix.
non-obvious takeaways: Airtel's AI is embedded in 30% of code written internally—unprecedented for telecom—and is driving 135M customer actions/quarter; solarization of 42,000 sites is a hidden cost hedge; Nxtra's Google partnership is a de facto sovereign cloud anchor, not just colocation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Wireless penetration in Rajasthan and the North-East still lags the national average, leaving significant headroom for long-term growth

- The regulatory environment remains constructive - TRAI has provided a stable and enabling policy framework while remaining responsive to industry concerns

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Annual Report sections routed here do not disclose a discrete plant or project pipeline - Bharti Hexacom is a licensed telecom services operator offering mobile, fixed-line telephone, Wi-Fi and IPTV across the Rajasthan and North-East circles, and the expansion agenda is expressed as a widening of the permitted business scope rather than as a physical capacity build. The principal forward step is a Special Resolution placed before the 31st AGM (Tuesday, August 11, 2026) to amend the main object clause of the Memorandum of Association, substituting sub-clause 1 of Clause III(A) so that the Company may establish, operate, maintain or expand telecommunication networks under the Telecommunication Act, 2023 across a materially broader set of services. The proposed clause explicitly covers unified and access services (mobile and fixed line/wireline), satellite-based telecommunication services, wireless and wireline access networks, internet services, national and international long-distance and international SIM services, internet telephony, enterprise communication, leased circuits and Internet Lease Lines, Machine-to-Machine (M2M), DTH and IPTV, Aeronautical Data Communication, In-Flight and Maritime Connectivity (IFMC), Captive Non-Public Networks (CNPN), PMRTS, cloud-based EPABX and Wi-Fi services, and captive telecom services. It also extends to telecommunication infrastructure activity as an Infrastructure Provider (IP) and Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Provider (DCIP) - dark fibre, rights-of-way, duct space, towers, poles, IBS infrastructure and associated equipment for wireline access networks, Radio Access Network (RAN), WLAN and transmission links - plus establishing and operating Internet Exchange Points (IXPs), Satellite Earth Station Gateways (SESGs) and related baseband systems, Network-as-a-Service (NaaS), Cloud-hosted Telecommunication Networks (CTNs) and CTN-as-a-Service, mobile number portability, and future-generation services such as 5G and 6G including OTT/multimedia delivery, satellite-based, cloud-native, virtualised, software-defined, non-terrestrial, AI-enabled and quantum-safe offerings. On the asset side, the Company operates a rolling programme of physical verification of fixed assets structured to cover all items over a period of three years, with network equipment moved between site locations on an urgent basis to keep the network running and each movement's situation subsequently updated in the Fixed Assets Register; customer premises equipment, bandwidth and optic fibre cable are not physically verified given their nature and location. Funding-side flexibility is being preserved through a Material Related Party Transactions approval with holding company Bharti Airtel Limited under Regulation 23(4) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, also tabled at the 31st AGM.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
